I think it misses an important facet of the pro-gun argument, which is that many see just the legality of weapons is a deterrent to violence. That is, that even if you hate guns, have never owned one, and will never own one, you benefit from living in a society were guns are legal, because a would-be attacker can't know you don't have a firearm. Advocates point to incidents in 'victim disarmament zones' as proof.

I think there's an attempt in the article to gloss over those parts of the discussion with phrases like "We will not discuss that arguments of what ifs", but ultimately the gun control argument is entirely a discussion of "what ifs". It's a big, complex issue, that's influenced by a lot of other factors that make correlations hard to link. For instance, we've made very few national changes to our gun policy since the 80's, but there's been a huge decrease in all violent crime, including gun-related homicide, over the last 20 years, despite what gets news coverage.
